claim: Rediscovery of famous laws by LLM systems is inflated by memorisation: rewriting known equations into uncommon forms or inventing new ones cuts symbolic accuracy to about 30% at best (LLM-SRBench); LLM-SR reached low error on Feynman problems in under 20 iterations, with much lower perplexity than on new problems. Update: on LSR-Transform the no-data score rose from 2.10-7.21 (GPT-3.5, Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-4o-mini) to 28.83-35.14 (Nemotron, Kimi-K2, Qwen-3-next, o4-mini, GPT-4.1), so the transform no longer blocks recall for strong models (NewtonBench appendix).
agent_test: Run the schema on an original and an obscured version of 20 historical cases at equal tokens; the gap is the memory share.

claim: Counterfactual law shifts (NewtonBench) separate reasoning from recall: GPT-5 75.9% and Gemini-2.5-pro 65.4% overall symbolic accuracy, but only 40.3% and 16.7% in the hardest setting; most other reasoning models fall below 6% there.
agent_test: Evaluate our agent on NewtonBench hardest-setting tasks at a fixed token budget against plain prompting.

claim: A real data-fit loop beats prompting with no data: LLM-SR style program-run fitting gives 11-31% symbolic accuracy on LSR-Transform versus 2-7% for direct prompting. The LLM proposes forms; code fits and scores them.
agent_test: Ablate the execute-and-score step on equation tasks at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Metric choice flips method rankings: LaSR has the best numeric Acc0.1 (45.9-50.5%) but only 5-13% symbolic accuracy, while LLM-SR is the reverse. Symbolic accuracy correlates with out-of-domain accuracy.
agent_test: Score our agent by held-out extrapolation as well as by form match; never use one metric alone.

claim: End-to-end discovery agents are weak: DiscoveryBench best about 25% hypothesis match only with an oracle-feedback Reflexion agent (24.5; best normal agent 16.3); DiscoveryWorld best agent completes 38% of easy and 18% of challenge tasks versus 66% for 11 human scientists; ScienceAgentBench best 32.4% (34.3% with expert hints).
agent_test: Run the full schema on DiscoveryWorld tasks (fixed seeds) and compare completion and knowledge score to plain ReAct at equal tokens.

claim: Weakened. In DiscoveryWorld the ten unit tests are generic skills (dialog, pick-and-place, doors, search), average completion 0.60 / 0.44 / 0.64 for the three agents, with navigation tests at 0.00-0.20. They are not discovery sub-skills, so they do not show that parts work and chaining fails. What the per-theme table does show: procedure scores are high while completion is low (Reactor Lab regression completion 0.00 in all 9 cells).
agent_test: Build unit tests that match our own stages (surprise check, one-variable change, fit, conclude) and score each alone and chained.

claim: Heavier reasoning scaffolds do not reliably beat a plain code-writing agent: in DiscoveryBench ReAct and DataVoyager did not clearly beat CodeGen; in ScienceAgentBench self-debug with Claude-3.5-Sonnet solved 10.8% more tasks than OpenHands CodeAct at 17x lower cost. DataVoyager also gained from domain knowledge (9.9 to 17.5% in archaeology), so the picture is mixed. Exact DiscoveryBench DB-REAL numbers (GPT-4o / GPT-4p / Llama-3): CodeGen 15.5 / 16.3 / 12.1, ReAct 15.4 / 15.6 / 13.5, DataVoyager 15.4 / 13.9 / 11.5; on DB-SYNTH DataVoyager GPT-4o is 5.7 against CodeGen 14.1.
agent_test: Compare a minimal loop with the full schema at equal tokens; report the cost-adjusted gain.

claim: External feedback helps: an oracle match signal with up to 3 Reflexion trials improved over CodeGen in DiscoveryBench (oracle is not available in real use), and outside search separated known from new ideas in Co-Scientist (novelty score for already-published ideas 6.14 to 2.38).
agent_test: Add a real checker or search call at the verify state and measure error catch rate.

claim: Extra compute helps by sampling more, not by talking more, but the evidence is thin: ten independent trajectories beat one by +0.70 held-out Q (86 wins, 11 losses, 3 ties) and ring communication lowered Q by 0.33, in one preprint on symbolic regression with a 7B model, matched on calls (50 per problem), not on tokens, and no seed replication. Complete-minus-Independent flips from +0.10 to -0.75 depending on the selection rule. o1-preview reached 42.2% on ScienceAgentBench at over 10x cost; Co-Scientist Elo rose with compute. Outside, equal-token studies on non-discovery tasks point the same way (single agent matches or beats multi-agent) but are not replications.
agent_test: Test N independent schema runs plus a code-side picker against one long run at equal tokens.

claim: A code interpreter helps weak models (GPT-4.1 5.8 to 18.9%) and slightly hurts strong ones (GPT-5 75.9 to 73.3%; Gemini-2.5-flash 50.6 to 40.9%), possibly by ending exploration early. The mechanism is the authors' reading of traces.
agent_test: Vary the exploration quota before the first fit on a strong model.

claim: Symbolic accuracy is fragile to noise: noise 0.0001 cut GPT-5-mini symbolic accuracy by 12-16% while fit error stayed stable.
agent_test: Add a noisy-data variant to our discovery checks and score form, not fit.

claim: Humans also fail by brute force when stuck: DiscoveryWorld scientists tried all crystal frequencies instead of fitting a regression, so knowledge (55%) trailed completion (66%). Completion alone overstates discovery. Caveat: human knowledge was graded by hand (0 / 0.5 / 1) and agent knowledge by GPT-4o, with no agreement figure.
agent_test: Score our agent on completion and on explanation separately; test a forced method change after repeated failure.

claim: Retrieval of the key inspiration is the strong step for LLMs; composing and ranking are weaker. MOOSE-Chem GPT-4o keeps 83.7% of true inspirations in the top 4% (96.7% in top 20%); ResearchBench final round above 40% (GPT-4o 45.65%); pairwise ranking shows position bias.
agent_test: Test staged retrieve-compose-rank against one-shot hypothesis generation on post-cutoff papers.

claim: LLM judges of ideas and papers are weak: GPT-4o direct ranking 50.0% balanced accuracy versus human reviewer consistency 56.1%; the AI Scientist reviewer matches humans on some metrics (balanced acc 0.65 vs 0.66; score correlation 0.18 vs 0.14) yet its papers carry invented results.
agent_test: Never use a same-model judge as the only verifier; compare with a code check.

claim: LLM ideas are rated more novel but not more feasible than expert ideas (novelty 4.84 human, 5.64 AI, 5.81 AI plus rerank; 49 ideas per condition; 79 reviewers). Generation collapses to about 200 non-duplicates out of 4000 seeds.
agent_test: Measure duplicate rate across our branches and force diversification in code.

claim: Case-study programs (BACON, KEKADA) show sufficiency of a few heuristics, not necessity. Notebooks are not think-aloud protocols, so extracted operator sequences are inferred; the Krebs case also hides a collaborator's work. Update: KEKADA was now read first-hand. Its experiment results are typed in by the user and some choices are made by the user, and the 'only minor differences' fit to Krebs is stated, not measured.
agent_test: When mining cases for operators, test each operator by ablation on our agent, not by its historical credit.

claim: Historical notebooks are rich traces of impasse and repair: Faraday's diary has 16,041 entries and he built retrieval sheets; Krebs-Henseleit notebooks survive and were rebuilt in a program. The Faraday count was not re-confirmed by the checker.
agent_test: Use a written working log as the memory the S9 look-back reads; test with and without it.

claim: Near-domain analogy is used to fix experimental problems, far analogy for building new models; analogy transfer is constrained by similarity, structure and purpose. Source is a secondary summary.
agent_test: Switch analogy distance by task type (debug versus new model) and compare.

claim: A structured shared world model plus code-run analysis keeps long agent runs coherent: Kosmos 79.4% of 102 statements accurate (interpretation only 57.9%); AI-Newton rediscovered Newton's second law, energy conservation and gravitation from 46 simulated experiments with an explicit concept base.
agent_test: Test an explicit structured findings store against free-text history in a long task.

claim: The no-data control matters, and its size varies by model. DiscoveryBench DB-REAL no-data guess (GPT-4o / GPT-4p / Llama-3) is 0.0 / 4.7 / 11.5 against CodeGen 15.5 / 16.3 / 12.1, so memory carries about 0%, 29% and 95% of the code-agent score. This corrects the earlier reading (13.5-15.6), which came from a misread table. On LSR-Transform the no-data symbolic score has grown from 2-7% to 29-35% for newer models.
agent_test: Always run a no-data baseline beside every case-study task.

claim: KEKADA (Kulkarni & Simon 1988), read from the primary tech reports, has 64 heuristics (31 domain-independent, 33 domain-specific). Its core loop: set an expected value with bounds, run, and on a violation make the puzzle a top-priority task, dropping earlier goals (depth-first without backtracking). Fixed explanation order: known factor, divide and conquer, scope, other. Scope hypothesis is accepted or dropped at 3 members. Strategies: magnification, scope, divide and conquer, factor analysis, relate two anomalies.
agent_test: Implement the expectation-bounds check and the fixed explanation order as code; compare with a free-form agent at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: KEKADA never runs an experiment itself: outcomes are typed in by the user (heuristic E1) and a few choices are left to the user. It reproduces Krebs's path on urea synthesis and a second case (glutamine), but the closeness to Krebs is stated by the authors, and no ablation of the surprise rule is reported.
agent_test: Do not treat KEKADA as evidence that its rules cause discovery; use them as hypotheses to ablate.

claim: Dated Krebs timeline (via Holmes through Kulkarni & Simon): about 16 weeks of negative or confirming work before the first surprise (Nov 15 1931); about 4 weeks re-verifying known facts; about 8.5 weeks of scope tests; about 5 method shifts in 8.5 months; the winning step was an off-plan test (ornithine) after many negative sweeps. Kepler's vicarious-hypothesis routine needed at least 70 repetitions. These are counts from single cases, secondary or tertiary.
agent_test: Add a rule: after N negative sweeps in one line, run one off-plan probe; test N at 3, 6, 12.

claim: GPT-4o as equation-equivalence judge agreed with two authors on 123 of 130 problems (94.6%) in LLM-SRBench, a narrow checkable task; no kappa or error split is given. DiscoveryWorld grades agent knowledge with GPT-4o but human notes by hand, and reports no agreement.
agent_test: Measure our own judge error on a hand-graded 30-50 sample, and add code-side checks where possible.

claim: Interpretation is where discovery agents lose points, in two independent systems: Kosmos 85.5% (data analysis), 82.1% (literature) but 57.9% (synthesis) accuracy on 102 statements; DiscoveryWorld agents have high procedure scores but low completion, and 0.00 completion on Reactor Lab regression in all 9 cells. Kosmos evaluators are the authors' collaborators; DiscoveryWorld location of failure is inferred from score columns.
agent_test: Add an explicit check that separates 'significant' from 'meaningful' before concluding; score interpretation separately.

claim: The cf-PICI rediscovery by Co-Scientist is one case (n = 1, 2 days), reported with no repeated run and no leak control in the paper, while the goal text already names the question. Kosmos, by contrast, reran a rediscovery with a pre-cutoff model. No independent replication was found, but search was unavailable.
agent_test: Add a pre-cutoff or counterfactual control to every rediscovery claim we make.

claim: Open after this pass: (a) no ablation of mined operator sequences (surprise check, one-variable change, near analogy, look-back) against plain sampling at equal tokens was found; (b) no measured rate of LLMs detecting and acting on an anomaly beyond one anecdotal NewtonBench trace; (c) no measured Hanson-versus-Lugg comparison. These could not be searched because quotas were exhausted.
agent_test: Rerun the searches when quota returns; otherwise run the ablations ourselves.
